title: Tactical release train: cut criteria, milestone alignment, and release-notes orchestration for API/Console/Runtime
creator: Olivia Chen
description:
Purpose: produce an actionable, time-boxed runbook for the Q2 release train that defines milestone dates, scope-lock checkpoints, objective cut criteria for API/Console/Runtime, and a single source of truth for release notes coordination. Goals: 1) minimize last-minute scope churn; 2) ensure release notes and docs are complete and verified before the public announcement; 3) align rollback/fallback criteria and cross-team owners.

Core deliverables:
- Milestone calendar with hard scope-lock and verification windows for each product area (API, Console, Runtime).
- Cut criteria checklist per component (functional regressions, perf regressions, critical bug count, security block).
- Release-notes orchestration playbook: owner assignment, contributions process, localization windows, final signoff.
- Communications plan for internal stakeholders (sales, support, solutions) and external release cadence.

Milestones (proposed):
- Feature freeze (soft): 2025-03-18 — last day for new features to be proposed; must include owner + feature flag plan.
- Code freeze (hard): 2025-03-25 — only fixes allowed; all PRs must reference release ticket and pass runtime tests.
- Docs & RN draft due: 2025-03-27 — initial release notes draft in Confluence and PR to docs repo.
- Verification window: 2025-03-28 to 2025-03-31 — cross-team verification and signoffs.
- Release go/no-go: 2025-04-01 09:00 PT — final decision at release readiness meeting.

Cut criteria (component-specific highlights):
- Runtime: no high-severity perf regressions detected vs baseline (p50/p95 token latency within 10% of target), KV-cache correctness tests green, memory leak P0s resolved.
- API: no security or auth regressions, end-to-end compatibility with common SDKs (Python/Node) verified, error rate <0.5% on staging load tests.
- Console: dashboard rendering regressions none critical, rollout and canary flow tested, role-based access checks pass.

Criteria for delaying release: any of the following triggers a delay to next ship window:
- A P0 regression that affects production path with no validated mitigation.
- Security vulnerability classified as High or Critical without an available patch/workaround.
- Sustained perf regression (p95 > 20% over baseline) discovered in smoke tests after code freeze.

Release notes orchestration: roles and responsibilities:
- RN Owner (PM): Ravi Kapoor — consolidate inputs, maintain canonical Confluence draft, final signoff.
- Eng leads (API/Runtime/Console): provide one-paragraph summary, user impact, and testing notes by 2025-03-24.
- Docs owner: Maya Torres — convert draft into docs repo PR, schedule localization pass.
- Marketing comms: Jonah Patel — prepare announcement draft and cadence for external channels after RN signoff.
- Support playbook: Priya Nair — create KB articles for migration/known issues.

Process for contributions to release notes:
1) Engineers open a lightweight RN submission in the RN tracker spreadsheet (link below) with owner, short description, and risk level.
2) PM consolidates and requests clarifications.
3) Docs repo PR created for each RN section; reviewers include eng lead and docs owner.
4) Final signoff by RN Owner and Eng Director.

Communication & gating:
- Weekly syncs (Tue 10:00 PT) during the run-up (Mar 11–Apr 1) with rotating owners.
- Daily standups in final verification week (Mar 28–Mar 31).
- Final go/no-go meeting agenda: health dashboard, open P0/P1s, RN status, support readiness, rollback plan.

Rollback and fallback plan (short):
- Primary: gradual rollback to previous runtime version in dedicated pool; API traffic shifted with smart routing in increments (10/30/60/100%).
- Fallbacks: enable read-only or reduced-throughput mode for Console; toggle feature flags where available.
- Postmortem: any critical delay or rollback triggers a blameless postmortem within 72 hours.

Trade-offs and open questions:
- Trade-off between longer verification window (reduces risk) and business need for faster release (marketing windows). Decision: prefer one-week verification but prepare contingency for a 1-week slip.
- Perf thresholds: teams asked to confirm whether 10% p95 tolerance is acceptable. Action: ENG leads to confirm by 2025-03-10.

Artifacts and links:
- RN tracker spreadsheet (canonical): https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASES/Q2-2025-RN-Tracker
- Release runbook draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/RELEASES/Q2-2025-Runbook
- Docs PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/docs/.github/PR_TEMPLATE.md

Success criteria for this ticket:
- All milestone dates published to stakeholders and calendar invites sent.
- Component cut criteria agreed and documented.
- Release notes draft complete and PRs opened in docs repo by due dates.
- Go/no-go decision process validated with a dry-run during the verification window.
